basis: Malignant neoplasm arising in skin; metastatic sites are not intrinsic organ involvement across this umbrella.
Classic Timothy syndrome is defined by long QT and syndactyly; neurodevelopmental impairment affects approximately 70-80%.
Adrenal failure, dystrophic myopathy and severe developmental delay define disease; megacystis 80-99%. Hepatic steatosis 30-79% omitted at cap; megalocornea need not impair vision.
Benign smooth muscle tumor arising in the small intestine.
Glycosylation disorder with defining skeletal and anterior eye abnormalities; hydronephrosis reported in 1/1 patient, supporting renal involvement with limited frequency certainty.
APRIL deficiency causes common variable immunodeficiency; no consistently damaged additional organ is established here.
Inherited cerebellar dysfunction; anemia and deafness belong to particular subtypes rather than most patients across the umbrella.
Pulmonary arterial vasculopathy with right heart dysfunction; reduced DLCO reflects vascular disease. Small selected phenotype subsets do not establish other common organ damage.
Adrenal steroid synthesis deficiency; structural urethral hypospadias is frequent (30-79%). Salt wasting itself reflects hormone deficiency, not intrinsic kidney damage.
Severe neonatal metabolic disease commonly causes fatty liver, cardiomyopathy and cystic renal dysplasia; neurologic and muscular manifestations omitted at the four-axis cap.
Dystrophy of the corneal epithelium; ocular location defines the disease even when visual impairment is absent.
Bacterial infection with variable anatomical sites; normal intestinal colonization does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Congenital uterine malformation confined to the reproductive system.
Disseminated fungal infection; destructive cutaneous lesions occur in most cases. Bone, pulmonary and CNS disease are variable and not established above 30% across the group.
Dermatophyte infection directly involves keratinized skin, hair or nails.
Benign adipose tumor arising in the esophagus; aspiration-associated respiratory infections are separate complications.
Diffuse astrocytic neoplasm arising in the central nervous system.
Defined by congenital recurrent laryngeal nerve paralysis, bilateral eyelid ptosis and loss of vocal cord function; laryngomalacia is also very frequent.
Renal tubular and electrolyte disorder with sweat gland dysfunction; alacrima 13/13 supports ocular involvement. Salivary dysfunction with xerostomia 13/13 omitted at cap.
Defined by pulmonary valve stenosis and congenital nephrosis; valve disease is cardiovascular.
Localized benign osteoma occupying the middle ear; no generalized skeletal disease is established.
Familial compressive median neuropathy; the TTR association alone does not establish systemic amyloid organ involvement.
Skeletal muscle channelopathy causing myotonia; potassium sensitivity does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Mixed glial neoplasm arising in the adult brainstem.
Jaffe-Campanacci phenotype combines multiple nonossifying bone fibromas and characteristic cafe-au-lait pigmentation; other organ abnormalities are not established as common.
